Edge AI · CPU-only · 4–6 GB Container

Edge Inference Engine + Sidecar Agent

An OpenAI-compatible LLM inference server that runs quantized small models entirely on CPU, paired with a LangGraph conversation agent in the same container — sidecar topology for sub-millisecond loopback hops, higher TPS, and lower tail latency than calling a remote model API.

What's Built

Five Composable Pieces

All five run end-to-end today: a CPU inference engine, a multi-turn LangGraph agent, two React UIs (a banking app + an ops dashboard), and a SQLite-backed observability layer with live SSE feed.

⚡

Inference Engine

Pure-Python llama-cpp-python server with OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions & /v1/completions. Streams tokens via SSE.

  • Gemma-2-2B-it · Q4_K_M GGUF
  • OpenBLAS-accelerated CPU build
  • Hot model swap (RLock-protected)
  • Single-flight semaphore per model
  • Configurable ctx · threads · batch
🤖

LangGraph Agent

Multi-turn conversational agent built on StateGraph with MemorySaver checkpointer. Calls the engine over loopback as a sidecar.

  • Per-session memory (UUID checkpoint)
  • System prompt injected at call-time
  • SSE token-by-token streaming to clients
  • langchain-openai ChatOpenAI client
  • Lives in same container as engine
📊

Observability Middleware

Pure-ASGI middleware (non-buffering, safe for SSE) records every request. Shared SQLite-WAL store between engine + agent processes.

  • Per-request: source · endpoint · model · tokens · latency · status
  • Thread-safe SSE event bus (call_soon_threadsafe)
  • /metrics/stats · /metrics/requests · /metrics/stream
  • Volume-mounted SQLite for restart durability
📱

NexaBank Mobile UI

React banking app whose landing page streams a personalized "Daily Insights" summary token-by-token from the on-device model.

  • 3 accounts · 10 transactions · 5 activities
  • Mobile-first 430 px phone frame
  • Vite proxies /inference & /api
  • Async-generator SSE consumer
📈

Observability Dashboard

Recharts-powered React dashboard shows live KPIs, requests/min, latency, token usage, and a tail-able request feed via EventSource.

  • 15 min · 1 h · 6 h · 24 h windows
  • P50 / P95 latency · error rate
  • Source × endpoint × model breakdown
  • Live request feed (SSE)
🛡️

Process Supervisor

Bash entry-point supervises both Python processes; if either dies (OOM, crash, anything), the container exits non-zero so Docker's restart policy fires.

  • wait -n on both children
  • SIGTERM → SIGKILL escalation
  • Healthcheck on both ports
  • ~15 s end-to-end recovery (verified)
Why Sidecar

Sidecar Topology = Higher TPS, Lower Latency

The inference engine and the LangGraph agent share a Linux network namespace inside one container. Every model call is an in-host loopback round-trip — no DNS, no TLS handshake, no public-internet egress, no cross-AZ hop, no per-request auth header round-trip with a hosted provider.

Loopback RTT
< 0.1 ms
vs ~25–80 ms public API
First-token latency
~1.5 s
P50 measured · gemma-2b Q4
Memory budget
6 GB
container limit · CPU only
External egress
0 bytes
PII never leaves the host
📡 Remote model API
  • Every call traverses TLS + cross-AZ + provider's queue
  • 30–150 ms network overhead added per call before first token
  • Per-request HTTPS / auth handshake (or pooled but capped)
  • Throughput capped by provider's TPM & rate-limit class
  • Cold-start penalty visible to user during traffic bursts
  • Sensitive data leaves the trust boundary
  • Egress bandwidth becomes the dominant cost line
🔌 Sidecar (this build)
  • Loopback hop; zero TLS, zero DNS, zero egress fees
  • First-token latency ≈ pure model compute time
  • Connection-pool stays warm inside the same kernel
  • Throughput limited only by CPU cores you give it
  • No cold start — model stays resident in process memory
  • PII never crosses the container boundary
  • Cost = the CPU you already pay for
Net effect on the agent path

A LangGraph node call to llm.invoke() resolves the inference HTTP request inside the same process tree. The 50–100 ms of network + auth + queue you'd spend per turn against a hosted provider becomes ~0 ms — which directly raises tokens-per-second under load (because the next request starts the moment the previous one finishes draining) and drops P95 because the long network tail is gone.

Streaming code
export async function* streamDailySummary(signal) {
  const r = await fetch('/inference/v1/chat/completions', {
    method: 'POST', signal,
    body: JSON.stringify({ stream: true, ... })
  })
  for await (const chunk of readSSE(r.body)) {
    yield chunk.choices[0].delta.content
  }
}

Architecture

One Container, Two Processes, Shared Everything

The supervisor entry-point boots the engine first, waits for /health, then boots the agent. Both processes share the loopback interface, the SQLite metrics file, and the same OOM cgroup.

Tech Stack

Boring Stack, Production-Friendly Choices

Every piece is something you can run on a laptop or a $20/mo CPU box — no GPU, no cloud-vendor lock-in, no opinionated framework on top.

LayerTechWhy
Inference runtimellama-cpp-python + GGUF Q4_K_MPure CPU, OpenBLAS-accelerated, hot-swappable models
Default modelgoogle/gemma-2-2b-it (~1.6 GB Q4)Strong instruction-tuning at the smallest tier that still feels coherent
HTTP frameworkFastAPI + Starlette · UvicornNative async, SSE-friendly, OpenAPI for free
API surfaceOpenAI-compatible /v1/*Drop-in for any OpenAI SDK or LangChain ChatOpenAI client
AgentLangGraph StateGraph + MemorySaverMulti-turn checkpointed memory keyed by session UUID
Agent → Enginelangchain-openai ChatOpenAIStandard interface; sidecar swap is a base_url change
StreamingSSE (text/event-stream)Token-by-token, browser-native, no WS handshake
ObservabilityPure ASGI MW + SQLite WAL + SSE busNon-buffering (safe with streaming responses); shared file across processes
FrontendsReact 18 · Vite · TypeScript · RechartsTwo SPAs (banking + dashboard) behind Vite dev proxy
ContainerDocker multi-stage · Python 3.12-slimOpenBLAS compiled in stage 1, slim runtime in stage 2
Process supervisionbash wait -n + signal trapsIf either child dies, the container exits and Docker restarts
PersistenceDocker named volume · SQLite WALMetrics survive restarts; readable concurrently from both processes
Roadmap

Next Steps

Where this goes from a working sidecar prototype to something you'd actually deploy as a fleet.

NEXT

Continuous batching & KV-cache reuse

Wire llama.cpp's n_parallel + dynamic batching so multiple in-flight requests share decode passes. Today each request holds the model semaphore — fine for a single banking app, blocking under fan-out. Should ~3–5× TPS on the same CPU.

NEXT

Speculative decoding with a draft model

Load a 0.5 B draft model alongside gemma-2b to draft 4–8 tokens per step and verify with the main model. With CPU-only inference this typically yields 1.5–2× wall-clock speedup on long generations.

SOON

Per-request token-level cost & budget caps

Extend the metrics schema with caller identity (API key) and start enforcing TPM + daily token caps inline at the middleware. Today metrics are observe-only.

SOON

Prompt cache (semantic hash)

Add a cosine-similarity cache layer in front of /v1/chat/completions for high-cardinality reads (status snippets, FAQ-style questions). Hits cost zero CPU.

SOON

Tool use in the agent

Wire LangGraph tool nodes for get_balance, list_transactions, find_card — backed by the existing mock data and eventually the real banking API. Lets the model answer "Did my paycheck land?" with the actual answer instead of a generic summary.

LATER

Multi-model registry & LRU eviction

Today the engine loads one model at boot. Add a registry that lazy-loads on first model= hit, evicts least-recently-used when memory is tight, and exposes /v1/models with live VRAM/RAM accounting.

LATER

Horizontal fan-out (Kubernetes DaemonSet)

The current "container per host" sidecar model maps directly onto a DaemonSet — every node runs one engine, every app pod talks to localhost:8080. Tail latency stays bounded because there's never a network hop.

LATER

Guardrails layer

Plug in the existing PII / prompt-injection regex stack (from the AI Gateway project) as middleware in front of /v1/chat/completions, so the sidecar enforces the same posture every app would otherwise re-implement.

LATER

OpenTelemetry export

Mirror the SQLite metrics into OTLP traces/metrics so the data plugs into Grafana, Honeycomb, or whatever the rest of the platform already runs. SQLite stays as the offline / debugging fallback.
